desc:
You are given points, a list of [x, y] pairs sorted by x in strictly increasing order. For two points i < j with xj - xi ≤ k, define its value as

y_i + y_j + |x_i - x_j|

Return the maximum value over all such pairs. At least one pair satisfies the gap condition.

points = [[1,5],[3,1],[4,8],[8,2]], k = 3
(1,3): 5 + 1 + 2 = 8
(3,4): 1 + 8 + 1 = 10
(1,4): 5 + 8 + 3 = 16   (gap 3)
(4,8) has gap 4 > 3 and is not allowed
result = 16
constraints: At least one pair of points has x<sub>j</sub> - x<sub>i</sub> ≤ k
hints: Checking all pairs is O(n<sup>2</sup>), which is already acceptable for 4,000 points, but try to find a linear approach. Start by removing the absolute value.
Since the points are sorted and i < j, |x_i - x_j| = x_j - x_i. The value becomes (y_i - x_i) + (y_j + x_j).
For each j you want the largest y_i - x_i among earlier points with x_j - x_i ≤ k. Keep a deque of earlier points whose y - x values are decreasing; drop the front while it is too far left.
editorial: Because the points are sorted by x and i < j, the absolute value disappears: the value of a pair is (y_i - x_i) + (y_j + x_j). The two parts separate, so for every j we only need the maximum of y_i - x_i over earlier points that are within horizontal distance k.

The set of eligible earlier points is a window whose left edge moves right as x grows (x is increasing). Maintain a deque of earlier points ordered so that y - x decreases from front to back. For a new point j: pop the front while x_j - x_front > k; if the deque is not empty, update the answer with front(y - x) + y_j + x_j; then pop from the back every point whose y - x is not larger than the new one and push j. Every point enters and leaves once: O(n) time and O(n) space.
